title: Add outcome-check, no-empty-success and thrash-stop standing defaults
summary: Add three cross-cutting standing defaults (outcome check with a fresh-reader rating of at least 4/5, no success from an empty list, stop on thrashing after two failures) to defaults.toml. Make the reader record them as acceptance criteria without asking, and show with tests that an explainer-page request receives them. The audience is the user and the reader role.

defaults_applied.how: Defaults are tested by parsing and rendering; loop enforcement is explicitly marked prose-only.
Criteria run tests that show the explainer request receives the defaults, not that entries merely exist.
New tests in athena-data; cargo test and clippy must pass.
One change: three defaults, one prompt line, tests.
Recovered the defaults format and render behaviour from the repository without asking.
Verifier runs the tests that exercise the explainer case.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience: the user and the reader role, who read the rendered defaults list; the explainer-page demonstration is a test, since the verifier cannot call a model.
An explainer page is class docs, so the new defaults must apply to docs; '*' is chosen because the rules are cross-cutting.
Enforcement of the 4-of-5 rating and the thrash stop in the loop code is not built; these are recorded as defaults and reader criteria, and marked prose-only for the loop mechanism.
defaults.toml version stays at 1 unless the parser or tests require a bump.
The three defaults come from the user's standing spec as stated in this request; source cites the request.

acceptance_criteria.text: defaults.toml gains three [[default]] entries with unique ids (outcome-check, no-empty-success, thrash-stop), each applies_to ["*"] (or classes that include docs), each with a source citing this request, and each statement's first sentence states the core rule, since render shows only that sentence.

The outcome-check statement says: the outcome is the check behind the work, not the activity; for audience-facing quality a fresh model reader that took no part in the work rates the live result as a newcomer, and a rating below 4 of 5 blocks completion. no-empty-success says an empty queue or finished list never counts as success alone. thrash-stop says that if the same item fails twice in a loop, the loop stops and reports thrashing.

The reader prompt (crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md) tells the reader to record applicable standing defaults of this kind as acceptance criteria and not to ask the user about them unless the request says otherwise.

Run `cargo test -p athena-data`: a new test loads the repository defaults.toml, selects defaults for class docs (an explainer page request), and shows the three defaults appear in the rendered default list; the existing parse, duplicate and render tests still pass.

Run `cargo test` for the workspace: a new test builds the reader brief for the request 'write an explainer page' and shows it contains the three defaults and the instruction to turn them into acceptance criteria, with no question field required; a rival check shows a request that says otherwise is not forced to carry them if the reader prompt supports that wording.

out_of_scope: Implementing loop code that actually computes the 4-of-5 rating or detects thrashing
Calling a live model in tests
departures: Slightly lower acceptance and verification: governance file change plus a demonstration test whose form is ambiguous.
